description_evaluated: Full playbook for a Replit Designathon competition submission — canvas organisation for judges, artifact selection, dual deployment (Replit Publish + GitHub Pages), session-to-session narrative continuity, and building-in-public commit discipline. Activate for "designathon", "competition", "building in public", "judges", "showcase", "submission", "dual deploy", "GitHub Pages + Replit", or any request to prepare a Replit project for public or competitive review.

queries.query: Prepare this Replit project for a Designathon submission
queries.rationale: Names 'Replit', 'Designathon', and 'submission' explicitly — a direct match to the description's core purpose and trigger keywords.

queries.query: Organize the canvas so competition judges can review the work
queries.rationale: Combines 'competition', 'judges', and canvas organisation for judge review — squarely within the described canvas-for-judges scope.

queries.query: Which app, deck, and video artifacts should judges see first?
queries.rationale: Artifact selection for what judges see is explicitly named in the description ('artifact selection', 'judges').

queries.query: Set up dual deployment on Replit Publish and GitHub Pages
queries.rationale: Matches 'dual deployment (Replit Publish + GitHub Pages)' verbatim, plus 'dual deploy' and 'GitHub Pages + Replit' trigger phrases.

queries.query: Make the commit history tell a clear building-in-public story
queries.rationale: Directly invokes 'building-in-public commit discipline' and the 'building in public' trigger keyword.

queries.query: Create a short handoff so the next Designathon session keeps the narrative
queries.rationale: Maps to 'session-to-session narrative continuity' plus the 'Designathon' keyword — clear match.

queries.query: Run a pre-submission showcase check for public review
queries.rationale: Contains 'submission', 'showcase', and 'public review' — three signals aligned with the description's activation clause.

queries.query: Switch the Replit canvas from building mode to judging mode
queries.rationale: The building-vs-judging canvas distinction and canvas organisation for judges are central to the description; Replit context reinforces it.

queries.query: Keep both public URLs visible to competition reviewers
queries.rationale: Two public URLs is the dual-deployment outcome, and 'competition reviewers' matches 'competitive review' and 'judges'.

queries.query: Audit the submission checklist and provenance before judges arrive
queries.rationale: 'Submission' and 'judges' are explicit triggers; provenance/checklist is part of the described pre-submission playbook.

queries.query: Deploy a regular Vite app to GitHub Pages only
queries.rationale: GitHub Pages appears, but the request is single-surface deployment with no competition/judging/Replit-Publish context. Description scopes GitHub Pages only as the dual-deploy half; mechanics belong to the vite-github-pages skill.

queries.query: Publish this internal app on Replit
queries.rationale: Replit Publish is mentioned, but 'internal' signals no public/competitive review. Description activates for public or competitive review, not routine internal publishing.

queries.query: Organize canvas frames for an internal engineering meeting
queries.rationale: Canvas organisation overlaps, but the audience is an internal meeting, not judges or competitive review — outside the description's activation context.

queries.query: Write a social-media launch post about building in public
queries.rationale: 'Building in public' keyword appears, but the task is marketing copy, not commit discipline or Replit submission prep. Keyword overlap alone is insufficient.

queries.query: Suggest conventional commit messages for a normal private repository
queries.rationale: Commit messages overlap with commit discipline, but 'normal private repository' contradicts the visible, building-in-public, judge-facing framing of the description.

queries.query: Create a pitch deck for an investor meeting unrelated to a competition
queries.rationale: Pitch deck overlaps with an artifact type, but the query explicitly disclaims competition context — the description activates for Designathon/competition, not investor decks.

queries.query: Produce a marketing video for an existing product launch
queries.rationale: Video overlaps as an artifact, but a product-launch marketing video has no judge/submission/Replit context that the description requires.

queries.query: Write a session handoff for routine backend maintenance
queries.rationale: Session handoff overlaps, but 'routine backend maintenance' lacks the Designathon narrative-continuity context; the description's handoffs are for multi-day competition builds.

queries.query: Set up dual deployment for a non-Replit project
queries.rationale: 'Dual deploy' keyword matches, but 'non-Replit' removes the Replit Publish half that defines this skill's dual deployment. Not applicable.

queries.query: Prepare this pull request for an internal code review
queries.rationale: 'Review' appears, but internal code review is unrelated to public/competitive submission review; no canvas, artifacts, dual-deploy, or judging signals.

method: Each query was judged solely against the supplied description text, not the skill body. Triggering required alignment with the description's stated purpose (Replit Designathon/competition submission prep) or its activation context (public or competitive review), beyond mere keyword overlap. Positive negatives were retained where a keyword appeared but the surrounding context (internal, private, non-Replit, non-competition, marketing) placed the request outside the described activation scope. true_positive = should_trigger true and triggered true; false_negative = should_trigger true and triggered false; true_negative = should_trigger false and triggered false; false_positive = should_trigger false and triggered true. recall = TP/(TP+FN); precision = TP/(TP+FP). passed = recall >= 0.85 AND precision >= 0.80.
